summary: Hope's Last Day 2/4 (Level 2 rooms → Tannen's Casino → Landing Pad → Other Areas → EVENTS) translated. Built as a verified transform of the English source: 117 exact replacements, each asserted to fire exactly the expected number of times, so every tag, class, style, src, data-uuid, data-hash and structural NBSP is carried over untouched by construction rather than by re-typing. All 19 headings translated and given an explicit id= carrying the original English slug (including the three that pre-baked data-hash links in this pack actually target: tannens-casino, a-cry-for-help, events). Three life-cycle names with no Chinese precedent (Drone / Chestburster / Ovomorph) were needed; I reused the project's own recorded Phase-0 coinages rather than inventing new ones, and used each in exactly one form throughout.

glossary_gaps.why: One of the six life-cycle names PROJECT.md §7.2.0 declares unsettled. Occurs 5× in this unit ('a Drone Xenomorph', 'a Drone', 'Drones', 'the Drone', 'Drone Xenomorphs'). I did NOT coin anything new: 工蜂异形 is the Phase-0 value already recorded in glossary_alien.pending.json, so the wave converges instead of diverging. Used in exactly this one form, never abbreviated to bare 工蜂. Note for the ch.10 ruling: English 'drone' in bee terminology is the male 雄蜂, not the worker 工蜂 — 工蜂 came from the wiki's loose hive metaphor. If the owner reopens this, 工兵异形 keeps the caste sense without the entomological error.

Same §7.2.0 status. Occurs 4× (Morgue event, Komiskey's birth, Lin's birth, The Birth event) plus once as the link label 'Stage III: Chestburster'. 破胸体 is the recorded Phase-0 value and is also the form PROJECT.md's own illustrative sequence (卵 → 抱脸虫 → 破胸体 → 成体) uses, so it is the lowest-divergence choice.

Same §7.2.0 status. Occurs once in prose and once inside the link label 'Stage I: Ovomorph (Egg)', which I rendered 第一阶段：异形卵（卵） — mirroring the English's own technical-term-plus-plain-gloss structure, with 卵 for the settled bare noun Egg. The Chinese redundancy is real but it is the English's redundancy; if ch.10 gives Ovomorph a distinct morphological form (e.g. 卵形体), that label should be revisited together with the J09 heading it points at.
Not needed by this unit — recorded only so the controller knows I did not silently touch the other half of the ladder.

open_issues: CROSS-UNIT LABEL SYNC (highest value to check): three of my seven link labels point at headings that live in units I do not own, so my label and that unit's translated heading must end up identical or the link text goes stale. They are — data-hash="stage-i" → 第一阶段：异形卵（卵） and data-hash="stage-iii" → 第三阶段：破胸体, both targeting h3 headings in ST-J09; and data-hash="final-horrors" → 最后的恐怖, targeting the h2 FINAL HORRORS in ST-J09. data-hash="sterile-lab" → 无菌实验室 targets a heading in ST-J07. The controller should diff these four against ST-J07/ST-J09 when both land.

Conversely, three data-hash anchors written in OTHER units point INTO my headings (tannens-casino, a-cry-for-help, events). I gave all three the exact English slug as id=, so they resolve regardless of what the other translator writes as the label.

Register note, not a defect: DO-NOT-TRANSLATE's heading_anchor_hashes lists stage-i, stage-iii and tannens-casino as 'not resolving today' in starterset — i.e. they were already broken upstream in the English. My id= on the Tannen's Casino h2 fixes one of those three as a side effect; the other two depend on ST-J09.

The four armory weapons appear in my table cells as prose (M4A3 制式手枪 / M240 焚烧器 / 阿玛特 37A2 型 12 号泵动霰弹枪 / 阿玛特 M41A 脉冲步枪). The same four exist as Item documents that will be T-BILINGUAL, and corerules ch.5 carries @UUID{Label} links whose labels must equal those Item names. My prose should match the Chinese half of whatever the Item names become — worth one pass at assembly time. 'Armat' transliterated 阿玛特 by the Seegson=西格森 precedent.

Brand/model policy I applied, flag if the controller wants it different: company names transliterated (Armat 阿玛特, Lockmart 洛克玛特, Pauling 保灵), alphanumeric model designations kept Latin, and the shuttle model 'Starcub' kept Latin under T-LATIN rather than coined — corerules already ships an Actor named 'STARCUB SHUTTLE', so coining a Chinese name here would pre-empt that unit.

'Pauling Surgical & Scanner MedPod' → 保灵外科 & 扫描医疗舱. I kept the & entity rather than replacing it with 与, to preserve both entities in the file; if house style dislikes an ampersand between Chinese words, 保灵外科与扫描医疗舱 is the drop-in alternative.

The h3 'Life Support/Power' got id="life-support/power" — that slash is the true Foundry slug (slugify is non-strict and only strips quotes). It is valid HTML5 and Foundry reads heading.id directly rather than via a CSS selector, so it is safe; noting it only because it looks unusual.

Register-vs-runbook nuance: PARALLEL-RUNBOOK §5 says evblockquoteCenter is read-aloud. In THIS unit that class carries no read-aloud narration at all — it wraps the THE MEDPOD rules sidebar and the three NPC stat blocks. I wrote them as GM-facing reference prose, and gave the atmospheric register to the actual scene descriptions (Ops, Medlab windows, the Morgue burst, the cascade of bodies) instead. Osterman's <em> line is the only spoken text and is voiced colloquially.

Terms I resolved from glossary_alien.json rather than the lang lock, listed so a reviewer can spot-check: Supply rating → 余量等级, Stretch → 节, Facehugger → 抱脸虫, Xenomorph/Xeno → 异形, Hadley's Hope → 哈德利的希望, Weyland-Yutani → 韦兰德-汤谷公司 (W-Y → 韦汤), Medlab → 医疗实验室, MedPod → 医疗舱, Stasis → 休眠, Keycard → 钥匙卡, Cutting Torch → 切割炬, Motion Tracker → 运动追踪器, Hive → 虫巢, Air Duct → 通风道, Company Agent → 公司代理人, Science Officer → 科学官, Newt → 纽特, Stage I/III → 第一/第三阶段.

One deliberate English-side liberty: the source says 'motion detector' twice, but the device is the pack's Motion Tracker item, so I used the settled 运动追踪器 both times rather than coining a second name for the same object.
